newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil central bank silent on Bamerindus report.
newsitem.headline: Brazil central bank silent on Bamerindus report.

text.p: The Brazilian Central Bank Monday declined to comment on a newspaper report that said it was looking for a new manager for ailing private bank Bamerindus.
"We have no comment on this report," said a Central Bank spokesman.

The Gazeta Mercantil financial daily said the Central Bank wanted to replace Bamerindus majority shareholder Sen. Jose Eduardo Andrade Vieira with a new manager and sell off the bank by December 1997.

The report said the central bank wanted profits, if any, from the sale to be distributed to shareholders and said that the deal could benefit from special credit lines under the PROER program for encouraging bank mergers.
Bamerindus, Brazil's fourth largest private bank, has been the target of takeover speculation for some time.
